title: Web Designer Intern (m/f/d)
description:
Most of the internet looks the same now. Help us make sure our corner of it doesn't.

Cloud Studios is a product studio in Berlin. We build our own products and grow the strongest into companies. Our whole idea fits in one line: build what should exist.

We're looking for a Web Designer Intern to own how our websites look, feel and work. Ours, and our clients'.

What you'll work on

A wide range of work, across several brands at once:

  • Our own sites. The Cloud Studios and GetMOW websites are live, and they're never finished. You'll redesign pages, sharpen what's there and add what's missing.

  • Launches. We have new products in the pipeline. When one is ready to meet the world, you'll design the site it meets the world on, often starting from a blank page.

  • Client websites. We also design and build websites for clients. You'll take projects from first idea to live site, and help present them.

  • The details nobody asked for. Motion, interactions, the 404 page, what happens when you hover. That's where a website stops looking like everyone else's.

By the end of your internship, you'll have several live websites with your name on them.

Ownership, for real

You won't be pushing pixels on someone else's mockup. You'll get a brief, sometimes just a problem, and the freedom to answer it your way. You'll work directly with Eli, our founder, from the first idea to launch day, and see your work go live in weeks, not quarters.

That freedom comes with responsibility. If you think a page is wrong, say so and redesign it. Nobody here will ask you to stay in your lane.

About AI

Anyone can generate a website now. That's the problem. The internet is filling up with sites that look like they all came from the same prompt, and we're not hiring someone to make more of them.

We use AI every day, and we'd love it if you do too: to explore faster, prototype faster and build things you couldn't build alone. But the idea has to be yours. Your taste, your references, your weirdness. We want work that nobody could copy by typing the same prompt.

If something in your portfolio has made someone ask "how did you do that?", we want to see it.

Who you are

You've designed websites before, and you can show us. Client work, a side project, your own portfolio, a site for your friend's band: live sites count for more than concepts.

You have opinions about type, layout and motion. You notice when something is a few pixels off, and it bothers you. You'd rather make something strange that works than something safe that nobody remembers.

You'll need:

  • Experience designing websites, and a portfolio that proves it.

  • Strong skills in Figma or a similar design tool.

  • A real eye for typography, layout and motion.

  • Good English, written and spoken.

  • To work independently. You'll manage your own time and projects, whether you're at home or in the office.

Bonus points:

  • You build what you design: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, ideally with a framework like Astro or Next.js. Design comes first, but designing and building is the dream.

  • You've designed or built with AI before, and you have an opinion on where it helps and where it doesn't.

  • There's something in your portfolio you made purely because you wanted it to exist.

  • German.

What you get

  • Ownership early. Real websites, real clients and real launches, from your first week.

  • Creative freedom. We give you problems, not pixel specs.

  • A portfolio that's actually live. Websites real people use, not concepts in a Figma file.

  • Founder-level access. You work directly with Eli, and you see how a studio launches products.

  • Work from anywhere in Germany. Remote is fine. If you're in Berlin, or want to be, there's a desk for you at our office.

  • Compensation. This is a paid internship.

  • A way in. If it's a great fit, the conversation towards the end of your internship is about staying on.

How we work

  • Execution beats perfection. We ship, learn and improve. We don't wait for perfect.

  • Be a sponge. Learn from everyone, every project and every mistake.

  • Agency is a skill. Nobody hands you the next step. You find it.

  • Say it directly. We tell you what we think, and we expect the same back.

Who you'll work with

You'll work directly with Eli Cloud Läufer, who founded Cloud Studios in Berlin in autumn 2025, and alongside Öykü, our product designer, and Jenna in marketing and design.

Who can apply

You must live in Germany and be currently enrolled at a German university or in vocational training in Germany, and one of these must apply to you:

  1. Mandatory internship (Pflichtpraktikum): your study or training regulations require you to complete an internship. You'll need to confirm this with your enrollment certificate and your program's internship requirement.

  2. Voluntary internship alongside your studies: up to three months, and only if you have never interned at Cloud Studios before.

If neither applies to you, we unfortunately can't consider your application.

Details

  • Duration: Three to six months (mandatory internship) or up to three months (voluntary internship).

  • Working hours: 20 to 40 hours per week.

  • Location: Remote from anywhere in Germany, or from our Berlin office. You don't need to be in Berlin.

  • Start date: As soon as possible.

  • Compensation: Included.

How to apply

Apply through our application form. It takes about ten minutes. The most important part is your portfolio, and the one project in it you'd fight for.

Show us something nobody else would have made.

title: Web Design Manager
region: San Francisco, CA / New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Web Design Manager at Anthropic, you will lead the enterprise web design team responsible for how businesses experience Anthropic on the web. Our website is often the first place enterprise buyers encounter Claude, and the pages your team ships need to make complex, technical products feel clear, distinctive, and trustworthy. You'll bring a strong art director's eye to every project, set the craft standard, shape design direction for the next stage of our enterprise web presence, and build a team that does the best work of their careers.

In this role, you'll own the enterprise web design practice: setting priorities, guiding projects from brief to launch, and holding a high bar for visual quality, storytelling, and performance. We're looking for someone who cares deeply about craft and knows how to use art direction (imagery, typography, motion, and composition) to tell a clear, memorable story on every page. You'll partner closely with enterprise marketing as your main day-to-day collaborators on priorities, messaging, and launches, and work alongside web engineering, web strategy and growth, brand and creative, sales and customer teams, product, and external agency partners to ship work that is both beautiful and effective.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead and manage the enterprise web design team, including hiring, coaching, feedback, and career growth

  • Own the craft standard for enterprise web design, ensuring pages are distinctive, clear, and performant

  • Set clear priorities and ways of working for the team in partnership with marketing and design leadership

  • Guide projects from brief to launch, turning marketing asks into clear creative direction

  • Provide hands-on art direction across imagery, illustration, typography, motion, and layout so every page tells a cohesive, compelling story

  • Coach designers on craft and visual storytelling, giving specific, actionable feedback that raises the quality of the work

  • Partner closely with campaign, product, and segment marketers on messaging, launches, and day-to-day priorities

  • Develop the design direction for the next stage of Anthropic's enterprise web presence, in support of company goals

  • Partner with web engineering to ensure designs ship with high quality and strong performance

  • Collaborate with SEO, analytics, and growth partners to measure results, run experiments, and improve conversion

  • Present design work and rationale to stakeholders, explaining decisions simply and pushing back clearly when needed

  • Build consistency across channels in partnership with brand, creative, and copy teams

  • Manage external agencies and design partners on larger web projects

  • Track the performance of shipped work and use data to inform, not replace, creative judgment

Minimum qualifications

  • Have deep web design experience, including directly managing web or creative designers

  • Have a portfolio of shipped web work that demonstrates strong craft, storytelling, and a clear point of view

  • Have strong art direction skills and a sharp eye for detail, with experience directing visual concepts from idea to polished execution

  • Think like a storyteller, shaping narrative and pacing across a page or campaign so design carries the message

  • Have designed for complex, multi-audience websites at scale, ideally for technical or enterprise products

  • Can turn complicated products into pages that are distinctive and convert

  • Are comfortable holding a high bar on tight timelines and making smart tradeoffs under pressure

  • Work well with marketing partners, translating asks into direction and pushing back with clarity and care

  • Understand web performance and use data and experiments well, without letting metrics replace creative judgment

  • Enjoy building teams, giving direct feedback, and helping designers grow

  • Can explain design decisions simply to stakeholders across functions

  • Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience at companies known for exceptional web craft on technical products

  • Familiarity with enterprise buyer journeys and designing paths to conversion

  • Experience partnering with SEO, analytics, and growth teams on experimentation programs

  • A background working closely with engineers on design systems, performance, and implementation quality

  • Experience managing agencies or external design partners on large web initiatives

  • Strong writing or content design sensibility that strengthens storytelling on the page

  • Experience setting design direction during periods of rapid company growth

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$305,000—$385,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
